binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, equipped with the assumption that mu is a probability measure.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: There exists a selector i among five square/Gaussian-style condition tags, with i not equal to the centered linear-MGF tag.

For that selected i there exists a real K_in > 0 such that X satisfies the corresponding tagged predicate: either (a) X is measurable and mu{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K_in^2) for every real t >= 0; (b) X is measurable and almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p >= 1 the function |X|^p is integrable with integral at most (K_in sqrt(p))^p; (c) X is measurable and for every real lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K_in, exp(lambda^2 X^2) is integrable with integral at most exp(K_in^2 lambda^2); or (d) X is measurable, exp(X^2/K_in^2) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
conclusions: There exists a real K_out > 0 such that X is measurable and almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p >= 1, |X|^p (real power) is mu-integrable and its integral is at most (K_out p)^p.
mathematical_definitions: The antecedent selector type has five constructors in recursor order: Gaussian tail, square-root moment growth, squared-MGF window, one-point quadratic exponential moment, and centered linear MGF; the fifth is excluded.

The conclusion selector type has four constructors in recursor order: exponential tail, linear-in-p moment growth, absolute-value MGF window, and one-point absolute exponential moment; the conclusion fixes the second constructor.
All integrals are real-valued Bochner integrals with respect to mu and act as expectations on the probability space.
For real p, powers such as |X|^p and (Kp)^p use real exponentiation; exponent 2 uses ordinary squaring.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, let X be a real-valued function. If X satisfies at some positive scale at least one of four conditions—Gaussian decay of the tails, square-root growth of all moments of order p>=1, a local quadratic-exponential MGF bound, or a one-point quadratic exponential-moment bound—then X has some (not quantitatively related) positive scale K for which every real moment order p>=1 is integrable and obeys E|X|^p <= (Kp)^p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The premise is existential over the condition tag: it requires only one of the four permitted branches, not all four.
The centered linear-MGF branch is explicitly excluded, so that condition alone cannot witness the premise.
The input scale K_in and output scale K_out are separately existentially quantified; the proposition states no numerical relationship between them and no universal conversion constant.
Positivity and measurability are repeated inside the detailed predicates; the outer positivity conjuncts are therefore redundant but do not make the implication vacuous.
Moment orders p are arbitrary real numbers with p>=1, and the powers are Real.rpow rather than natural-only powers.
No centering, symmetry, independence, identical distribution, variance normalization, or relation to another random variable is assumed in any permitted premise branch.
The conclusion is only the linear-in-p moment formulation; it does not conclude any of the other three absolute-value/exponential-tail formulations.
ambiguities: The finite selector types and constructors are anonymized; their mathematical labels are recovered from the supplied recursor branch labels and dispatched predicate bodies rather than from source names.

The packet exposes the real Bochner integral through an opaque wrapper, but every active moment or exponential integral that matters to the translated conclusion is accompanied by an explicit Integrable requirement.
No quantitative dependence of K_out on the antecedent branch or K_in is encoded, so none can be inferred.
